core.title: Bind every declared acceptance to at least one test
core.given: A plan artifact declares one or more acceptances
core.when: the planner declares, edits or keeps an acceptance in the plan artifact (at any phase; the check is evaluated whenever it runs)
core.then: Every acceptance declared in a plan artifact is bound by at least one test of the stack.
core.why: An acceptance with no bound test cannot be executed or checked, so the plan claims behaviour that nothing proves.
evidence: The traceability closure check reports zero declared acceptances lacking a bound test.
verification: Checked by a traceability closure check that joins acceptances declared in plan artifacts against test bindings; it applies in every phase and is evaluated whenever it runs.
Strict disposition: every declared acceptance without at least one bound test is a finding; no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.
The concrete representation of an acceptance-to-test binding is whatever the stack's traceability closure check recognises; this rule defines no new binding format.

fires: A plan artifact declares an acceptance and no test is bound to it, whatever phase the work is in.
A previously bound test is removed or its binding changed so a declared acceptance is left without any test.
doesNotFire: Every declared acceptance is bound by at least one test.

profileRequirements.meaning: The syntax by which a test file binds itself to a declared acceptance, i.e. what 'bound by a test' means concretely.
profileRequirements.bunValue: verifier_detail[1]: 'The concrete representation of an acceptance-to-test binding is whatever the atdd_traceability_closure validator recognises; this rule does not define a new binding format.'

profileRequirements.meaning: Where plan artifacts live, so the check can find the acceptances a plan declares.
profileRequirements.bunValue: Not stated in bun.json; the atdd_traceability_closure validator scans the stack's plan tree.

profileRequirements.meaning: Which tests of the stack count as binding targets, i.e. what 'a test' means in the core obligation.
profileRequirements.bunValue: 'Bun test' (title and then): the runtime's built-in test runner, whose test files carry the bindings.

bunOnly.text: The atdd_traceability_closure validator reports zero declared acceptances lacking a bound Bun test.
bunOnly.reason: Names this rule's Bun validator id and the Bun test runner; the neutral core states the same evidence generically (the check reports zero unbound acceptances).

bunOnly.text: Implemented as a validator (ref: atdd_traceability_closure). Strict disposition: every unbound acceptance is a finding.
bunOnly.reason: The validator id is a realization detail of this one rule (notProfileKeys); only the strict disposition and the generic description of the check carry into core verification.

bunOnly.text: The concrete representation of an acceptance-to-test binding is whatever the atdd_traceability_closure validator recognises; this rule does not define a new binding format.
bunOnly.reason: Defers the binding format to the Bun validator by name; the core keeps the deference generically and takes the concrete syntax from profile key urn.binding.acceptance.

bunOnly.text: finding = acceptance-without-binding-test (observability: needs_new_observer): produced by the atdd_traceability_closure validator joining declared acceptances against Bun test bindings; its result is not exposed as an activation fact today.
bunOnly.reason: The finding id and its observer are realization details; it signals a violation, not a precondition, so the core keeps no finding fact and states the violation generically in verification (every unbound acceptance is a finding).

classification.note: Neutral already; 'a plan' is the plan-artifact role, whose location the profile supplies.
'the closure validator' is genericized to 'the check'; the no-phase-restriction and whenever-it-runs qualifiers are preserved in when and feed verification[0].

'Bun test' becomes 'a test of the stack' (which tests count comes from tooling.test_runner); 'bound' takes its concrete syntax from urn.binding.acceptance. The obligation is unchanged: at least one bound test per declared acceptance.

Neutral evidence drops the validator id and 'Bun'; the validator id itself stays bunOnly. How declared acceptances are identified for the join is owned by the closure check itself (kept as deference in core verification), not by any profile key.
Strict disposition (with the shared strict policy: fails on every finding, no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline) maps to verification; the validator ref and id are bunOnly.
The deference of the binding format is kept generically in verification; the named validator is bunOnly; the concrete binding syntax is supplied by the profile.
task_has_acceptance=true is stack-neutral and is the sole activation precondition; it applies in every phase, with no phase restriction.

Signals a violation, not a precondition; its finding id and observer are realization details, so the core keeps only the neutral precondition fact and describes the violation generically in verification.

neutralityNotes: The obligation neutralizes cleanly: 'bound by at least one Bun test' becomes 'bound by at least one test of the stack', with what counts as a test (tooling.test_runner), where plan artifacts live (roots.plan) and the binding syntax (urn.binding.acceptance) supplied by the profile; these keys exist in the closed vocabulary, so proposedKeys is empty. bun.json fixes no concrete binding syntax — the Bun validator owns it — so the core keeps the deference generically ('whatever the stack's traceability closure check recognises'). Likewise, the identity on which declared acceptances are joined to test bindings is left to the stack's closure check: bun.json establishes no acceptance URN shape, so urn.acceptance is deliberately not used. The validator id atdd_traceability_closure, the finding id acceptance-without-binding-test and its needs_new_observer status remain bunOnly. prefer, avoid and unless are empty in the Bun sidecar and stay empty; no examples were invented. The 'no phase restriction' qualifier is preserved in when, fires[0] and verification[0], and the removal/rebinding case is preserved in fires[1].
